# Capsule Examples

13 examples demonstrating Capsule across frameworks and bundlers. Every example has tab navigation (Home/Server or Native/Server) and working route files (`src/routes/hello.ts` + `src/server/routes/ping.ts`).

> Agent navigation: see `CONTEXT.md` (Layer 2 map). Build/run/test commands are owned by
> `../docs/contributing/commands.md`; emulator + env helpers are the repo-root `pnpm dev:*` scripts
> (`../scripts/`) — this file does not restate them.

---

Extended versions of the React template testing CSS, native APIs, routing, and more.

| Example | What's tested | Port |
|---|---|---|
| `react-ts` | **Canonical native-API demo** — Native tab (Device/Alerts/Haptics/Clipboard/Storage/Location/QuickJS) + Routes tab | 5173 |

> **Examples convention:** demo new native APIs in `react-ts` (feature-screen registry + `ui.tsx`).
> `react-ts-native` is a look-and-feel sandbox only — don't wire real APIs there.

## How dev mode works

**Vite examples**: Capsule wraps Vite programmatically — injects `<script src="/__capsule.js">` into every HTML page, proxies `/api/*` and `/_capsule/*` to the route sidecar on `devPort+1000`.

**Angular**: Capsule generates `.capsule/proxy.json` and passes `--proxy-config` to `ng serve`.

**Non-Vite bundlers**: Capsule starts a transparent HTTP proxy on `devPort` that:
- Injects `/__capsule.js` into HTML responses on the fly
- Forwards `/api/*` and `/_capsule/*` to the route sidecar
- Forwards WebSocket upgrades (HMR) to the bundler on `devPort+1`
- Sets `CAPSULE_INTERNAL_PORT` env var so bundlers use the shifted port

### Custom build tools

Non-Vite examples declare `web.devCommand` in `capsule.config.ts`:

```ts
// capsule.config.ts (webpack-preact)
web: {
  buildCommand: 'pnpm exec webpack --mode production',
  devCommand:   'pnpm exec webpack serve',
}
```

Vite-based examples rely on the default and don't need these fields.

> **Always use `capsule dev android`, not `pnpm run dev`** — only the former runs `adb reverse`,
> without which the device WebView can't reach your PC (`ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`).

## `react-ts` route demo (QuickJS + HTTP routes)

`react-ts` exercises on-device routing. Route features are **prod-mode only** — in `capsule dev`
the WebView talks straight to the bundler, so the embedded server/QuickJS don't run and the route
sections error gracefully.

| File | Type | Route | What it tests |
|---|---|---|---|
| `src/routes/quickJs.ping.ts` | JSON-RPC | `quickJs.ping` | Restores eval via JS route |
| `src/routes/custom.hello.ts` | JSON-RPC | `custom.hello` | File-based route override |
| `src/server/routes/ping.ts` | HTTP GET | `/api/ping` | embedded server (CivetWeb) → QuickJS routing |
| `src/server/routes/items.ts` | HTTP GET+POST | `/api/items` | In-memory list, persists per app session |

**Verify on a device/emulator** (build & install per `../docs/contributing/commands.md`; emulator via
`pnpm dev:emulator start` from the repo root):
1. **QuickJS Engine** — `Math.sqrt(144)` → Eval → `12`
2. **JS Route Override** — type a name → `Hello, <name>! (handled by QuickJS)`
3. **HTTP Routes → Ping** → `{ "status": "ok", "path": "/api/ping", "runtime": "QuickJS" }`
4. **HTTP Routes → Load** → `apple, banana, cherry`; type `mango` → Add → list grows (state persists)

## Setup

The examples are their **own pnpm workspace** (`examples/pnpm-workspace.yaml`, one
`examples/pnpm-lock.yaml`), separate from the framework's root workspace — so the root
`pnpm install` / `pnpm build` never pulls in 13 apps' framework dependencies. Each app links the
in-repo `@capsule/core` (`link:../../packages/core`), so build the framework first:

```sh
pnpm install && pnpm build     # repo root: framework packages (core + CLI)
cd examples && pnpm install    # every example at once (one lockfile)
```

**All examples at once** — use the batch helper from the repo root (don't hand-run loops):

```sh
pnpm dev:examples install                  # pnpm install (the examples workspace)
pnpm dev:examples build --release          # capsule build android --release in each
pnpm dev:examples test                     # pnpm test in each (skips apps with no test script)
pnpm dev:examples all                      # install -> build -> test
pnpm dev:examples build --filter react-ts  # only matching apps
```

Per-app build, run, dev, AAR-rebuild, and instrumented-test commands live in
**`../docs/contributing/commands.md`**; emulator lifecycle and per-machine env vars are the repo-root
`pnpm dev:emulator` / `pnpm dev:env` scripts (values in the git-ignored `.env.local`).
